S1_consent_precedes_storage.how_verified: Read (not trusted) the actual code path in apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink and apps/bot/src/handlers/companion.ts. Constructed the exact abandon-before-consent adversarial case: a brand-new guest (never seen by the bot) opens the i_<code> link. makeStartHandler runs resolveOrCreateUser (unconditional, pre-existing REQ-014 behavior identical across every /start entry point -- writes only tg_id/tg_username/lang, no name/phone/email/company; this write is not introduced by this diff and predates it). resolveInviteDeepLink then checks hasConsented; for this guest it is false, so the function shows the consent prompt and RETURNS immediately -- no invite_codes read (getInviteCodeByCode is called only after the hasConsented check, later in the function body, confirmed by reading the actual source, not the design doc's claim), no getProfileByUserId call, no Profile write, no Registration write, no AuditLog write. If the guest closes the chat here (never taps 'I agree'), zero new profiles rows and zero new registrations rows exist for that guest -- confirmed by tracing every write statement reachable from this branch (there are none). Only the pre-existing bare users row exists, which is not a personal-data write in S1's sense (S1's own negative-case list names a Profile row, not a User row, as the failure mode) and is unconditional platform behavior already reviewed under REQ-014, not something this diff introduces or could have avoided. If the guest taps 'I agree', consent:agree fires, recordConsent sets consent_pd_at (the one legitimate write at this point), and only then does resolveInviteDeepLink resume and run the codeRow/existingProfile read-only lookups. For a brand-new guest (existingProfile === null), the companion field-collection conversation (handlers/companion.ts) is entered. Traced makeCompanionTextReplyHandler line by line: on a parse failure it re-prompts with no write; on success it renders the confirm message via ctx.reply with no write. Traced makeCompanionConfirmCallbackHandler: it re-parses the tapped message's own text, re-reads the invite code (read-only), then calls redeemInviteCode -- the single write transaction. No DB write of any kind exists anywhere in the field-collection/confirm-message code path prior to that one call. This differs from REQ-019's write-as-you-go pattern by design and the code matches that design.
S1_consent_precedes_storage.note_for_test_designer: AC3 in GitHub issue #71 is worded 'ZERO new users rows, ZERO new profiles rows and ZERO new registrations rows for that guest.' Taken completely literally this AC does not hold: resolveOrCreateUser unconditionally inserts a bare users row (tg_id/tg_username/lang only) the instant a brand-new guest opens the link, before hasConsented is even evaluated. This is pre-existing REQ-014 platform behavior (identical for every /start, every deep-link kind), not something REQ-039 introduces, and it carries no name/phone/email/company -- the actual personal data S1's Profile-level consent gates. This is not a security defect and is not grounds for a FAIL here, but TEST-DESIGNER must scope the AC3 verification correctly (measure profiles/registrations tables, and treat the platform-baseline users row as expected/out-of-scope) or a literal reading of AC3 will report a false failure unrelated to this requirement's actual security property.

S1_returning_guest_race_backstop.how_verified: Independently re-read apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts:337-364 -- createWalkinProfile now takes an options param and, when { onConflictDoNothing: true } is passed, executes db.insert(profiles).values(values).onConflictDoNothing({ target: profiles.userId }) -- confirmed present in the actual code, not just claimed by the design. Confirmed the companion call site (apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts:774-794, inside redeemInviteCode's transaction) is the only caller passing { onConflictDoNothing: true }; REQ-030's own walkin call site (domain/walkin.ts's commitWalkin) is unaffected and still passes no options, so its behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. Outcome on conflict: no crash (onConflictDoNothing degrades the INSERT to a silent no-op, standard Postgres/Drizzle upsert semantics), the existing Profile row is left untouched (no clobbering of a returning guest's richer REQ-019 data), and the registration row is written regardless -- invitedByUserId: codeRow.grantsCompanionOf is set unconditionally at inviteCode.ts:809/824, independent of whether the Profile insert happened or no-opped. Registration correctness (AC1 attribution) holds in both branches.
